The `create-pluto` command makes a new project from a template.

## Run the CLI

::code-group
```bash [bun]
bun create pluto@latest
```

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm create pluto@latest
```

```bash [npm]
npm create pluto@latest
```
::

The CLI starts a setup wizard.

## The wizard

The wizard asks these things, in this order:

1. **Project directory.** The default is `my-pluto-project`. The CLI makes the directory if it does not exist.
2. **Website title.** The default is `My Awesome Website`.
3. **Database provider.** Choose `Supabase` or `None (Markdown files in GitHub)`.
4. **Supabase values.** Only for Supabase. See [With Supabase](#with-supabase).
5. **Template.** The list shows only the templates that the database allows.

| Database | Templates |
| --- | --- |
| Supabase | `Shop`, `Blog` |
| None (Markdown files in GitHub) | `Blog` |

If the database has only one template, the wizard picks it for you.

Before the download, the wizard checks two things. If `nuxt.config.ts` exists in the current directory, the wizard asks "Nuxt project detected. Do you want to add Pluto environment variables?". If the target directory is not empty, the wizard asks for confirmation.

You can cancel at any prompt.

## Skip the prompts

Pass the directory as the first argument. Pass a template shortcut with `-t`, `--template`, or `--template=`. The shortcut skips the database and template prompts. The directory argument skips the directory prompt. The wizard still asks for the website title.

```bash [Terminal]
bun create pluto@latest my-project -t supabase-shop
```

The shortcut has two parts: `<database>-<template>`.

| Shortcut | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `supabase-shop` | Supabase and the shop template |
| `supabase-blog` | Supabase and the blog template |
| `core-blog` | No database and the blog template |

The `core` database has only the `blog` template. A shortcut such as `core-shop` is not valid. An unknown shortcut is also not valid. In both cases, the CLI prints the available options and exits with status 1.

## What the CLI writes

The CLI downloads the template from GitHub with `giget`. The URL has this form:

```text
gh:plutocms/pluto-<database>-<template>-template
```

Then it writes a `.env` file. If `.env` exists, the CLI merges the new values into it. Each value is quoted.

The CLI always writes the website title:

- `WEBSITE_NAME` for the Supabase templates.
- `NUXT_PUBLIC_WEBSITE_NAME` for the `core` template.

### With Supabase

The CLI asks for three values. It checks each one.

| Prompt | Variable |
| --- | --- |
| Supabase URL | `SUPABASE_URL` |
| Supabase key | `SUPABASE_KEY` |
| Database connection string (`postgres://` or `postgresql://`) | `DATABASE_URL` |

You need a Supabase project first. You can make one at [database.new](https://database.new/). Find the connection string in the Supabase dashboard: Project Settings, Database, Connection string. The pooler connection string also works.

### With the core template

The CLI downloads the template. Then it asks for the GitHub App settings. Every prompt is optional. Press Enter to skip a prompt and fill the `.env` file later. When the terminal is not interactive, the CLI skips all these prompts and writes empty values.

| Prompt | Variable |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub repository (`owner/name`) | `PLUTO_CMS_REPO` |
| GitHub App slug | `PLUTO_CMS_APP_SLUG` |
| App ID | `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_GITHUB_APP_ID` |
| Client ID | `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` |
| Client secret (the input is hidden) | `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` |
| Path to the private key `.pem` file | `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY` |

The CLI reads the `.pem` file and writes it on one line. Each line break becomes a literal `\n`. The CLI never prints the key or the client secret.

The CLI also writes `NUXT_PLUTO_CMS_SESSION_PASSWORD`. The value is random and has 43 characters.

At the end, the CLI prints the next steps. Create a GitHub App, install it on the repository, fill the empty values in `.env`, and run the dev server. If you gave no repository, the steps also tell you to set `PLUTO_CMS_REPO`.

## Start the dev server

::code-group
```bash [bun]
cd my-pluto-project
bun install
bun run dev
```

```bash [pnpm]
cd my-pluto-project
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

```bash [npm]
cd my-pluto-project
npm install
npm run dev
```
::

Open `http://localhost:3000/admin`.

With the core template, the dev server reads and writes the local `content/` folder. On your machine, you are signed in as a local user. See [GitHub CMS](/github-cms).

::note
A normal project uses the npm packages and needs no setup for local layers. The `plutoLayer` helper and `PLUTO_LOCAL_ROOT` are for people who work on Pluto itself. See [Local layers](/contributing/workspace#local-layers).
::
